clue.text: Military government making poet cut grass

parts.note: Martial was a Roman poet famous for his epigrams

indicators.note: cut means the grass word loses its final letter, docked like a trimmed lawn

parts.note: a lawn is an area of mown grass

explanation.surface: A military regime is formed when a poet mows the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims the last letter from LAWN, leaving LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial law is rule by the armed forces in place of civil authority.

clue.text: Every old-fashioned person is clear of debt

parts.note: all means every one
a square is a conventional, unfashionable person

explanation.surface: Every conventional person manages to pay off what they owe.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits with nobody owing anything is an idiom for level or settled.

clue.text: Direction ending some musicians ' time off

definitions.text: Direction ending some musicians ' time off

parts.words: Direction ending some musicians ' time off
parts.note: a marking in a score telling players who have been resting during a solo passage that everyone now plays together

explanation.surface: An instruction that cuts short the players' break.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian term meaning all marks where the full ensemble rejoins after a solo, so resting players resume.

clue.text: Easy-going notice on a board about parking

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: about means the board phrase goes around the parking letter

parts.note: a gives the letter A
a table is a flat board
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A relaxed notice pinned on a board concerning parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts P inside A TABLE to give APTABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone flexible who adjusts readily to change is relaxed and accommodating.

clue.text: Having a sly look, on entering Ireland

indicators.note: entering means the Ireland word goes into the other piece

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone casts a sly glance as they arrive in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link word, but it is LEG, the cricket name for the on side of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Leering is looking at someone in a lascivious or knowing way.

clue.text: Dam and daughter like the Scottish sisters

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river

explanation.surface: A mother and daughter resemble Macbeth's witches.
explanation.walkthrough: The weird sisters are the three witches in Shakespeare's Scottish play, Macbeth. 'Dam' suggests a mother animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth's three witches are called the weird sisters, weird meaning fate-controlling and uncanny.

clue.text: Prepare to set off and run together

definitions.meaning: to fit a bomb or firework with a detonating cord so it can be ignited
to melt and blend into one, as metals do

explanation.definitionFit: Fitting a charge with a detonator readies it to explode; metals that melt into one another are said to merge in the same way.

clue.text: Planning for the future that assists one's aims

definitions.meaning: prudent anticipation of what is to come
the front sight on a gun barrel, which helps the shooter aim

explanation.definitionFit: Prudent anticipation is one sense; the other is the bead at the muzzle end of a rifle used in aiming.

clue.text: Way to show something in a case

definitions.text: Way to show something in a case

parts.words: Way to show something in a case
parts.note: a single step, which put in front of the word case makes a flight of steps, a way up or down

explanation.surface: A method of displaying an item in a glass cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step is part of a flight of steps, and put before case it names a set of steps leading between floors.

clue.text: Sluggish breed for the Derby, say

parts.note: flat means dull or lifeless, as sluggish trade is
a race is a breed or stock of animals or people

explanation.surface: A slow strain of horse is entered for the Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is the famous English horse race at Epsom run without jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is an example of a horse race on level ground with no fences.

clue.text: Raid no different from this?

indicators.note: different says the letters of the words before it are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about a raid being no different from something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' signals an anagram of RAID NO, and the whole clue is the definition: an incursion is indeed a raid.
explanation.definitionFit: An incursion into enemy territory is a raid, so the clue's question answers itself.

clue.text: Look for an opening in the church

definitions.meaning: a hagioscope, an oblique hole in a church wall giving a view of the altar

explanation.definitionFit: A glance with half-closed eyes is one sense; the other is the architectural term for a slanted aperture through a chancel wall.

clue.text: Application to work in commercial enterprise

definitions.meaning: manufacturing and business activity as a whole

explanation.definitionFit: Industriousness is diligent effort, and the same word names manufacturing and trade generally.

clue.text: Long story about an amusing person

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the pieces that follow are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an gives the letter A
a gas is informal for a highly entertaining person or thing

explanation.surface: A long tale is told concerning someone very funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns A GAS round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a lengthy narrative, originally an Old Norse prose epic.

clue.text: Wheezing in a match? It's calamitous

indicators.note: calamitous suggests the letters have been thrown into disaster and disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is gasping for breath during a game that has gone badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calamitous' rearranges A MATCH IT'S; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suffering from the respiratory condition that narrows airways breathes with a whistling sound.

clue.text: Head of department framed by bigger gun, perhaps in resentment

indicators.note: framed by puts one piece inside the other, which surrounds it like a frame
perhaps suggests the letters may be arranged some other way
Head of picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A department head surrounded by a bigger gun resents being outranked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gun' looks like a weapon, but with 'bigger' it is anagram fodder signalled by 'perhaps'; 'framed by' wraps it round D. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A begrudging attitude is one of grudging reluctance, so the word is used in the sense of a grudge or reluctant ill will.

clue.text: Not quite satisfied with a French domestic servant that's useless

parts.note: un is the French word for a
a help is a domestic worker

indicators.note: Not quite means the satisfied word loses its last letter

parts.note: full means satisfied after eating

explanation.surface: Someone is not entirely content with a French cleaner who is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the final L of FULL, leaving FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gives no assistance is of no use.

clue.text: Dreadful thing to spoil middle of sleep

definitions.text: Dreadful thing to spoil middle of sleep

indicators.note: Dreadful suggests the following word is mangled into a different order

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the five-letter word that follows

explanation.surface: A terrible thing ruins the middle of a night's rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' reads as the adjective of the definition but signals the anagram; 'middle of' picks one letter from 'sleep'. Read whole, the clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream is a frightening experience that wrecks a night's rest.

clue.text: It's reckless, for a start, to annoy hives

indicators.note: for a start puts the annoying word at the front, ahead of the reckless one

parts.note: to nettle is to irritate or annoy
rash means reckless or hasty

explanation.surface: Someone says that, to begin with, it is foolhardy to provoke a swarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hives' looks like beehives, but it is the itchy skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Hives is the everyday name for urticaria, an itchy skin eruption like that caused by stinging plants.

clue.text: Drink we must imbibe if we have fish

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: must imbibe means the we pieces swallow the following word, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: We have to drink if we want fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we have' is a link phrase; 'must imbibe' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The alewife is a North American herring-like species.

clue.text: Measure of insulation provided by clothes

definitions.meaning: a tog is a unit of thermal resistance used for duvets and clothing

explanation.definitionFit: Duvet warmth is rated in units called togs; separately the word is slang for garments.

clue.text: Fill old man in France full of food

indicators.note: full of means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: pere is French for father, the old man
meat is an old word for food in general

explanation.surface: A French father stuffs himself with food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old man' is slang for father; in France that is PERE. MEAT once meant any food.
explanation.definitionFit: To permeate is to spread through and saturate something, filling it throughout.

clue.text: Be stuck at first in the way out

indicators.note: in places the stuck letter within the way-out word

parts.note: an exit is a way out

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone is trapped right at the start of an exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives S, the opening letter of 'stuck', which goes 'in' EXIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, to have being.

clue.text: A dessert that's risen is withdrawn

indicators.note: that's risen means the dessert word goes up, read from bottom to top in this down entry

parts.note: a fool is a cold pudding of fruit puree and cream

explanation.surface: A pudding that has puffed up is taken off the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: FOOL is a British pudding of crushed fruit folded into cream; 'that's risen' turns it upwards to LOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved, distant person keeps apart from others, emotionally removed.

clue.text: Not altogether clean tools in shed

indicators.note: Not altogether says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Somewhat grubby implements are kept in an outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in shed' as the definition; 'in' is a link word, since the answer means shed, not 'in shed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple outbuilding propped against a wall, a type of shed.

clue.text: Courts in foreign country (not America)

indicators.note: not means the America letters are taken away from the country

parts.note: Austria is a country abroad from Britain

explanation.surface: Legal proceedings held abroad, excluding the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing US from AUSTRIA leaves ATRIA. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central courtyards in Roman houses or modern buildings.

clue.text: Writer goes across street into restaurant

indicators.note: goes across means the writing word spans the street abbreviation, holding it within

parts.note: a biro is a ballpoint pen, a thing that writes

explanation.surface: An author crosses the road to dine out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is a pen: BIRO is the British brand name for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal eating place.

clue.text: Natural grass in front of a lake

indicators.note: in front of places the earlier pieces before the lake abbreviation

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing on someone to the police
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A natural scene of grass beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is not the plant: in British slang it means to inform on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal behaviour is relaxed and unaffected, which is what natural means here.

clue.text: Origins of odd tinge in colour of ears

indicators.note: Origins of takes the beginning letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A strange tint appears in the colour of someone's ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective relating to the auditory organ, from Greek for that organ.

clue.text: Gunner's unpaid assistant, one depending on charity

definitions.meaning: a loader feeds ammunition to a gunner, and one working without pay is a free one
a scrounger who lives off others' generosity

explanation.definitionFit: A sponger who takes from others without paying is the second sense; the first splits the word into gratis plus the gun crew member who loads.
